findings.text: ACPI ITS translator discovery builds a memory window from the firmware record base plus a fixed ITS size, obtains a firmware domain token, binds it to the reported translation identifier, creates an ITS node with firmware provided NUMA affinity, marks non shareable when a recent firmware revision reports non coherent, then probes one ITS with ordered unwind of node and token on any failure.

ACPI ITS bring up first prepares firmware NUMA mappings, then resets every translator before probing any of them, proceeds to probe only when the reset scan observed at least one entry, and finally releases the firmware mappings; an alternate configuration provides empty probe and mapping helpers with NUMA reported as absent.

Top level ITS initialization creates an aligned table pool, caches redistributor state plus parent domain plus default priority, dispatches to flattened device tree or ACPI discovery, disables logical interrupts when no ITS appears, allocates logical interrupt tables, surveys version four capabilities across nodes, sanitizes an inconsistent virtual identifier flag, optionally establishes virtual processing element domains with version dependent signalling operations, and registers for system core suspend resume.

Logical interrupt memory reservation setup does nothing without firmware configuration tables or without discovered ITS nodes, otherwise installs a dynamic online processor hotplug step for per processor reservation and records the assigned step in shared redistributor state.

Version four enablement accepts a parent domain plus virtual element and signalling operation sets, caches them for later use and reports success, otherwise reports that no virtual element domain was allocated.
Redistributor region descriptor holds a mapped base pointer, the corresponding physical base address, and a flag indicating whether the region contains a single redistributor.

Chip context aggregates firmware handle, distributor physical and mapped bases, an array of redistributor regions with count and stride, embedded redistributor collection state, interrupt domain pointer, 64 bit flag word, range selection support flag, private interrupt count, and a partition affinity array with its count.
Partition affinity entry pairs a processor mask with a firmware identifier for the partition.

Architectural counts and defaults observed here are sixteen software generated interrupts, at most four T241 chips, a default processor mask register value of 240, and a driver log prefix identifying GICv3.
Integration workaround flags occupy the low four bits of a 64 bit word, one each for MSM8996 wake handling, Cavium erratum 38539, ASR erratum 8601001, and insecure integration.

Hardware interrupt numbers fall into disjoint classes covering low private and software generated values, a shared range below about one thousand, a 64 entry extended private window, a 1024 entry extended shared window, a large logical range starting at 8192 up to a 24 bit limit, and an invalid class for anything else; only software generated plus private plus extended private are treated as redistributor local.

Distributor capabilities derive identifier count as a power of two from the type register identifier bits, usable shared line count as the smaller of reported shared interrupts and 1020, and extended shared count from its dedicated type field.

Register access selects the current processor software generated base for redistributor local classes and the global distributor base for shared and extended shared classes, returning absent for other classes.

On systems affected by the T241 fabric issue, read accesses for shared interrupts are steered to one of four distributor aliases according to 320 entry groups, while extended shared interrupts always use the fourth alias; unaffected systems always use the single distributor base.

Register offset translation keeps classic identifiers unchanged, rebases extended private identifiers to continue after the private range, and for extended shared identifiers normalizes by the extended base while redirecting classic distributor operations to their extended counterparts; unexpected classes raise a programming warning.

Single interrupt masking and unmasking operate on one bit within a 32 entry word at a translated offset, using the per processor base for local classes and distributor bases for global classes, with masking followed by a register write pending drain on the affected interface while unmasking performs no drain; one deactivation mode additionally clears active state for interrupts forwarded to a virtual processor.

Generic interrupt state queries and updates are accepted only below the logical interrupt threshold and map pending, active and masked requests onto the corresponding set and clear operations, with masked assertion reusing the mask path and active assertion forcing a readback to ensure completion.

Non maskable promotion is available only when build and runtime pseudo NMI support are both present, is rejected for enabled interrupts and for logical identifiers, installs a distinct high priority for promotion and restores the normal priority on teardown, and switches only globally routed interrupts between fast non maskable and normal fast handlers.

Boot priority discovery samples implemented priority bits from the processor interface, probes group zero access by saving the mask register then testing whether a highest non zero priority survives a write read round trip, reads the distributor disabled security bit, attempts to force disabled security for broken insecure integrations when group zero is present and otherwise forbids non maskable support, caches both security observations, and converts distributor priorities to non secure form only when group zero exists without disabled security.

Redistributor power control is skipped entirely on one broken integration, otherwise it clears a sleep request to wake or asserts it to sleep, interprets lack of persistence as absence of power support, then polls a children asleep indicator until it matches the requested sense with bounded microsecond polling.

Write pending and redistributor wake or sleep timeouts only produce rate limited diagnostics and allow execution to continue, and an unrecognized interrupt class triggers a programming warning while preserving the original offset.

Per processor redistributor helpers resolve the current processor record, expose its control base, and derive the software generated base as a fixed 64KB higher mapping; an affinity helper extracts bits 4 through 7 of the affinity register value.
A specific ARM64 erratum workaround is required only when its runtime key is enabled and the interrupt is shared or extended shared with an effective affinity that excludes the executing processor.
Callers must already hold the interrupt descriptor lock when promoting an interrupt to or demoting it from non maskable handling.

Small helpers expose the hardware interrupt number directly from interrupt data and expose effective versus configured affinity masks, with a single processor fallback to processor zero when symmetric multiprocessing is absent.
Conversion of a distributor priority to its non secure representation is defined as a one bit left shift masked to eight bits.
Single ITS reset from firmware records builds a transient memory resource from the record base plus the fixed ITS window and delegates to the common single ITS reset operation.
